items.title: 56422_Leonard Phillips oral history interview
items.q: We used to get together and play Bix, Frankie Trumbauer... We played together, played it three-part harmony.

ctx.x: Was Lester into that? Was he listening to that?

Yeah, we used to listen to them, different things. Then after that, we got together, Lester, Pete and myself... We used to get together and play Bix, Frankie Trumbauer... We played together, played it three-part harmony.
We'll get to that a little later, because that's a little later on. But at this time, in 1924, on that first carnival tour, Lester was not listening to records, or was he listening to records?

items.title: 56422_Leonard Phillips oral history interview
items.q: See, Frankie and them made records with the small groups, where you could really dig 'em.

ctx.x: What about the Hawkins things that were on those Fletcher Henderson records? He was doing some things, wasn't he?

Hawkins didn't have too much out. See, the thing about Hawkins and them, Hawkins and them didn't play too much...only with the band. But see, Frankie and them made records with the small groups, where you could really dig 'em. See, you'd dig a cat when he's out there playing in the small group more than you can... That's why people dug Louis. You didn't have to hear Louis play 16 bars or 18 bars, or maybe a chorus in a band... That ain't like you're out there playing by yourself; I mean, playing the whole record.…
